# SK1102 — The local function is declared before the jump that ends the block

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A block whose last statement is a jump has one or more local function declarations written directly above it, so the declarations read as work done before the block is left.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | hint |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |
| ReSharper | `MoveLocalFunctionAfterJumpStatement` (`resharper_move_local_function_after_jump_statement_highlighting`) |

## Why

A local function declaration is not an executable statement, so the jump is the last thing the block does no matter where it is written. Moving the jump above the run puts the page in the order the program is in. ⚠ **Hoisting is what makes the move sound, and it is a stronger fact than "the jump is last"**: a local function may be called from above its own declaration, so `return Inner();` moved above `int Inner() => 7;` still binds. ⚠ **This is the only rewrite in the batch that cannot produce `CS0136`, because it introduces and removes no name at all** — nothing but the jump statement changes position, and a jump declares nothing. ⚠ **Nothing in the .NET SDK reports the shape.** On the same `net10.0` probe with every code-style diagnostic raised, a method holding a local function before its `return` drew `IDE0062`, `IDE0061` and `IDE0060` — all about the function, none about where it sits.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
Work();

void Work() { }

return;
```

Write:

```csharp
Work();

return;

void Work() { }
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **This rule is cosmetic and says so by shipping at `hint`** — Roslyn `Hidden`, reached only through `--include-hints` or an explicit severity. Nothing it reports is a defect and nothing it changes affects behaviour. The argument for spending an id on it is the one this tool exists for: a local function is the last thing added to a method and gets appended where the cursor was, which is why generated code carries the misordering far more often than hand-written code does. ⚠ **`goto` is deliberately not one of the jumps.** Every other jump has one destination the reader can see from the statement itself; a `goto`'s label may be anywhere in the member, including above the local functions, so "the block ends here" is not what the statement says — `SK7074` reports unstructured `goto` and this rule has nothing to add to it. The jump must be the block's last statement and must be directly preceded by at least one local function; the whole run of them is skipped in one move. ⚠ **Comments inside the local functions are untouched and that is the point of where the jump lands**: the fix inserts it at the start of the first local function's *full* span, above its documentation comment rather than between the comment and the declaration. The only comment at risk is one written above the jump itself, and that one withdraws the finding. A preprocessor directive anywhere in the reordered region withdraws it too, because the jump could move out of a conditional block it was inside or into one it was not. Generated code is excluded.

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK1102.severity`
